subject.title: fix #95279: Provide a trusted inbound-decoration contract so consumers can strip/dedup without forgeable text heuristics

question: Should trusted inbound-decoration state be a durable OpenClaw-owned transcript metadata contract, and if so should it live under the existing `__openclaw` envelope rather than as generic top-level message fields?
rationale: The reader plumbing is broad and persistence-sensitive, but the branch does not establish a canonical producer or a durable ownership/provenance boundary; choosing that contract is an architectural product decision rather than a mechanical follow-up.

options.title: Adopt an internal metadata contract
options.body: Define an OpenClaw-owned inbound-decoration record under `__openclaw`, populate it at the decoration producer, and update this PR to consume only that record.

options.title: Approve top-level fields as public contract
options.body: Document `inboundDecorated` and `bareBody` as durable generic message fields, define accepted producers and import semantics, and add compatibility coverage.

options.title: Defer the contract
options.body: Close or pause this implementation until maintainers choose a single serialized ownership model for trusted inbound bodies.

recommendation.title: Adopt an internal metadata contract
recommendation.body: Define an OpenClaw-owned inbound-decoration record under `__openclaw`, populate it at the decoration producer, and update this PR to consume only that record.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision crosses the shared transcript schema and its consumers; the supplied material does not identify a higher-confidence historical owner.
